content.content:
how a concept product can still use this grammar: every panel is operable
markup computing its state from data arrays in the page, and the page says on
its face that the scenario is a demo. What stays banned is the painting of a
surface, an image or dummy divs posing as something that runs. If the panels
cannot actually compute, the grammar is unavailable. Pick another.

---

### 2.4 Continuous world

One canvas, fixed for the entire scroll, and the page travels through it.
Waypoints, not sections.

> **This grammar REQUIRES worldflight mode.** `data-sc-mode="worldflight"`, one
> fixed stage, one spacer, legs that crossfade. See references/worldflight.md.
>
> Building it out of pinned acts is not a lesser version of this grammar, it is
> a different and worse page, and it has already been tried. The owner's verdict
> on the act-based attempt: "awful... you're literally going from scrolling down
> to static page and then you start scrolling down again... weird clear page
> lines scrolling up... very cheap looking." Every one of those is the same
> defect. A pinned act is a block in the document; a document made of blocks has
> seams; and a world with seams is not a world. Do not reach for `scrub` acts
> here, however long you make the spans.

**Fits:** a journey with real geography. A supply chain, a process with physical
stages, a place, a build, anything where "where you are" is meaningful.

**The scroll feels like:** moving through a single space that never cuts. The
visitor never leaves the frame.

**Forbids:** section boundaries of any kind. No `sc-section` blocks, no acts at
all, no second stage, no `drift` steps (one continuous grade across the whole
travel, authored into the world, not interpolated between legs). Nothing may
scroll *over* the canvas: copy arrives inside it, at waypoints, in the fixed
copy layer. The only element in document flow is the spacer.

**Nav, hero, close:** the nav is a **map**. A waypoint list, a depth readout, a
position marker, and it is clickable, because a world you cannot skip around in
is a video. The hero is an establishing position inside the world, not a
separate title stage. The close is arrival at a place in the same canvas, and
the CTA is an object in that place.

**Leans on:** worldflight legs with `data-sc-linger`, copy windows against the
whole track, the `sc:waypoint` event driving a rail the page draws itself.
**Bans:** every act device, `flow`, `pan`, hard cuts, `src` swapping.

**This is the expensive one.** The chain warning in SKILL.md applies: a single
unbroken flight is the most fragile thing you can build, and the seam law in
worldflight.md section 6 is not optional. Choose this grammar only when the
brief is literally about travel through a place, and budget for the reroll.

---

### 2.5 Typographic poster

Type is the imagery. Media is minimal or entirely absent, and scale contrast
does every job that photography would have done.

**Fits:** a brand whose asset is a sentence. Manifestos, agencies with strong
verbal identity, launches with one claim, anything where a stock-looking image
would weaken the page rather than support it. Also the right answer when there
are no good assets and generating them would produce eight plausible, forgettable
frames.

**The scroll feels like:** words arriving at wildly different weights. A word at
40vw, then a paragraph at 16px, then silence. Rhythm comes from scale, not
motion.

**Forbids:** photographic ground, `scrub`, scrims (nothing to scrim), cards of
any kind, and decorative motion. If a device is doing the work instead of the
typography, the grammar has already failed.

**Nav, hero, close:** the wordmark is set as part of the composition, at
composition scale, not as a 14px bar item. There may be no persistent nav at
all. The hero is a single word or one line at extreme scale, filling the
viewport, with a real `<h1>` behind it. The close inverts the whole page: the
smallest type on the site, the CTA as a plain underlined link, quiet after all
that volume.

**Leans on:** `kinetic` (this is the one grammar where character splitting can
be right), `pin` with scale driven from `--sc-p`, `reveal` as a wipe across
letterforms, `drift` doing heavy lifting because the ground is most of the
frame. **Bans:** `scrub`, `pan` rails of cards, `tilt`, `parallax` on text.

**The typography floor doubles here.** taste.md caps display at ~6rem outside a
hero moment. This grammar is one continuous hero moment, so the cap lifts, but
the tracking, measure and optical-correction rules tighten: at 40vw, default
tracking is a visible defect and one bad kern is the whole page.

---

### 2.6 Gallery / catalog

Objects in a walkable collection. Museum labels, not marketing copy.

**Fits:** a range. Products with variants, a portfolio, a menu, a materials
library, case studies, anything where the visitor's real question is "what are
the options" rather than "should I believe you".

**The scroll feels like:** walking a room. Lateral drift with vertical scroll,
objects entering and leaving at their own pace, each one labelled with fact
rather than pitch.

**Forbids:** the argument-shaped pinned type act; a single hero claim; scrim
copy over media; persuasion in the object labels. A label reads
`Cedar. Air-dried 18 months. Kiln-finished.` and not `Craftsmanship you can
feel.` Every object gets the same label schema, no exceptions, because the
schema is what makes it a collection instead of a grid.

**Nav, hero, close:** the nav is an **index of objects**, and it jumps. The hero
is object one, already in view, already labelled, with no separate title
treatment: the collection starts at the top of the page. The close is either the
last object or an inquiry plate typeset exactly like a label, so the ask reads
as part of the collection.

**Leans on:** `pan` as the spine rather than as one act, `reveal` per object,

# BRIEF — Eric Rash, personal site (scroll-craft build #1)

Interviewed 2026-09-02. Five of the eight answers are the human's own choices,
made in-session. Three are marked **self-authored** and were written from his
existing `~/DEV/Website/personal/BRIEF-V3.md` ("Night Field") because he was
explicitly working at low capacity and the skill permits a self-authored
fallback. Those three are flagged inline and in the final report.

---

## The eight interview answers

**1. Vibe in three to five words, plus references from any medium.**
*Self-authored, from BRIEF-V3.md.*
Quiet, exact, Texas, after-dark, instrumented.
References (non-web, per the skill's rule against naming sites):
- The instrument panel of a light aircraft at night — everything legible, nothing decorative.
- A Peter Saville record sleeve: one idea, enormous space around it.
- A stadium an hour after everyone leaves, floodlights still on.

**2. The scroll journey, section by section.**
*Self-authored, from the section headings of his live site, which are his own words.*
The question comes first → four checks before the first chart → what I actually
work with → how I work → get in touch.

**3. The energy curve.**
*Self-authored.*
Starts quiet and slightly tense. Tightens through the middle as the data side
gets denser and more insistent. Releases hard at the reframe. Ends quiet, but a
different quiet from the opening: settled rather than waiting.

**4. How should someone feel, stage by stage, and the ONE moment they remember?**
The one moment is **his own answer, chosen in-session**: *the question reframe.*
A wall of athlete data drains away and leaves one sentence standing.
Stage-by-stage feeling curve is below.

**5. One thing this site should do that no site they have seen does.**
Seeded by his choice of peak. Realised as the signature move below.

**6. How far from premium-minimal.**
**Premium-minimal.** His answer. Consistent with the kitsch ban in BRIEF-V3.md.

**7. One unbroken world, or distinct scenes?**
**Distinct scenes.** His answer. Worldflight is therefore out, and so is the
continuous-world grammar.

**8. What assets do they already have?**
**Nothing.** His answer. No photos, no footage, no brand imagery, and no
`KIE_AI_API_KEY` on the machine. He chose the code-drawn route over buying
credits. Every visual on this page is Canvas 2D or inline SVG, drawn in the
page. There is no video anywhere in this build.

---

## Grammar: Split stage

Two columns held in tension for the whole page, resolved by scroll.

**Why this one.** His thesis has two literal sides — *"Most performance problems
are not data problems. They are question problems."* Split stage is the grammar
for "any argument with two sides… the comparison is the product." Its mandated
close is the **collapse**: the divider travels to one edge, one column takes the
full width, and the CTA lives in the winning column. That collapse *is* the peak
he picked, unprompted. The grammar and the peak are the same object.

**Why the other seven lost.**

| Grammar | Why not |
|---|---|
| Filmic one-shot | Carries a burden of proof in this skill, and would need a scrub hero. No video exists. Its own strength — carrying the visitor — is wrong for a page whose point is that the visitor should stop and re-ask the question. |
| Chaptered editorial | Genuine runner-up. Fits a method or manifesto. Rejected because it has no structural home for the reframe: chapters cut, they do not resolve. The peak would become just another chapter opening. |
| Live surface | Requires panels that actually compute on real or clearly-labelled data. His real athlete data is identifiable health data and must never leave the machine. Without it the grammar's honesty rule makes it unavailable. |
| Continuous world | He explicitly chose distinct scenes over one unbroken world. Also the most fragile and expensive option, and there is no geography in the brief. |
| Typographic poster | Strong on "no assets", and nearly won. Rejected on loudness: it is one continuous hero moment at 40vw type, which contradicts his premium-minimal answer and his own kitsch ban. |
| Gallery / catalog | For "what are the options". His question is "should I believe you", which is the opposite. |
| Rhythmic cutlist | Speed and hard cuts. Directly against the quiet, exact vibe and the slow reframe. |

**What this grammar forbids, and I will honour:** full-bleed anything before the
resolve; centred copy; the corner-anchored hero; a symmetric close; either
column becoming decorative. Bans: `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, more than one
`scrub`, `drift`.

**Nav, hero, close, per the grammar:** No top bar. **The divider is the chrome**
— it carries both side labels and the progress of the argument. The hero
establishes the split at 50/50 on the first screen with both headlines readable
at once. The close is the collapse.

---

## The signature move: the divider is a force trace

The vertical divider between the two columns is not a rule. It is a live
**counter-movement jump force-time curve**, drawn in Canvas, running the full
height of the page, and its playhead position is driven off `--sc-p`.

- It is drawn from the real, known shape of a CMJ trace: quiet stance, the
  unweighting dip, the braking rise, the propulsion peak, flight at zero, the
  landing spike. Not a decorative wiggle. `taste.md` forbids fake data and his
  V3 brief carries a kitsch ban.
- As the argument advances, the trace advances. The visitor is scrolling through
  a jump.
- At the collapse, the trace **flattens to a single straight underline** beneath
  the one surviving sentence. The instrument stops measuring and becomes
  punctuation.

**Why this is not a reskin.** It is not a kit device with new parameters. It is
bespoke Canvas in the page, driven off the custom property the engine publishes.
The engine is not touched.

**Not a duplicate of his existing site.** `~/DEV/Website/personal/index.html`
already has a `trace-panel` the visitor drags as a slider. That is a widget
inside a section. This is the page's chrome, it spans the whole document, and
the visitor never grabs it — scroll drives it. Different object, different
interaction.

---

## The journey (beats)

| # | Beat | What shifts |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recognition | Both sides named. The visitor sees the split and understands the format before scrolling. |
| 2 | Accumulation | The data side thickens. More metrics, tighter packing, more insistent. |
| 3 | Strain | The data side is now overwhelming and still has not answered anything. |
| 4 | The reframe | **PEAK.** The data drains. One sentence stands. |
| 5 | Method | What replaces it: the four checks that come before the first chart. |
| 6 | Commitment | One action. Email. |

Six beats. Total span target **9.5 viewport-heights** — deliberately outside the
13.6–13.8vh / 6–7 act band that the skill records as a fingerprint of its own
first four builds.

---

## The feeling curve

Written before the score table, per `feel.md`.

| Act | Feeling | What on screen causes it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recognised, slightly on guard | Both headlines legible at once. Neither side is winning yet. The trace sits at quiet stance. |
| 2 | Busy. Mildly impressed. | The left column fills with real metric names. The trace enters the unweighting dip. |
| 3 | Oppressed. It is too much and it means nothing. | Left column at maximum density, still no answer. The trace hits the braking rise. Left column is now visibly louder than the right, and the right has gone almost silent. **This is the authored silence.** |
| 4 | Relief, then clarity. | The data drains. The divider travels. One sentence at full width. The trace peaks at propulsion, then goes to flight. |
| 5 | Grounded, practical | Four checks, plainly set. The trace lands. |
| 6 | Settled | The trace is a flat underline. One link. |

No two adjacent acts carry the same feeling. Act 3 is quieter on the right
precisely so act 4 is the largest change on the page.

**The peak:** act 4. It gets the largest span by a visible margin (2.6vh against
a 1.2–1.6vh average) and the silence in act 3 in front of it.

**Authored silence:** the right column in act 3 drops to a single short line with
a lot of space. The verification pass must not read this as dead scroll — the
left column and the trace are both still moving through it.

**The tell-someone sentence:**
*"It's the site where all the data drains away and leaves you with the question."*

---

## The score

| Beat | Device | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Recognition | `pin` + divider at 50/50 | The grammar requires both headlines readable at once before any movement. Pin holds the frame while the split is understood. |
| 2 Accumulation | `flow` + `in` | Items arriving on their own schedule is what accumulation *is*. No pinning — the page should feel like it is filling, not holding. |
| 3 Strain | `reveal` (per side) | A wipe is a change of state. The left side wipes to its dense state; the right wipes down to almost nothing. |
| 4 The reframe | `pin` + `--sc-p` divider travel | The peak. Frame holds absolutely still while the divider crosses the whole viewport and the data drains. Stillness is what makes the travel readable. |
| 5 Method | `flow` + `in` | Back to arriving, but slower and in one column. Same family as act 2 on purpose — by now it reads as resolution, not repetition, because the layout changed underneath it. |
| 6 Commitment | `pin` + pointer | The page stops moving and starts responding. Grammar bans `magnet`, so the pointer work is a subtle cursor-proximity warm on the mail link only. |

**Checks against the grammar and the skill:**

- Grammar bans honoured: no `pan`, no `spotlight`, no `magnet`, no `drift`, zero `scrub` (0 ≤ 1). ✓
- Four device families used: `pin`, `flow`+`in`, `reveal`, pointer. ✓
- No device family twice in a row: pin → flow → reveal → pin → flow → pin. ✓
- No two adjacent acts share a feeling. ✓
- One peak (act 4), largest span by a clear margin. ✓
- Total 9.5vh, six acts — outside the 13.6–13.8vh fingerprint band. ✓
- No `count` device anywhere: he has no real site statistics, and inventing them
  is banned. No number, no counter. ✓
- No `01 / 06` counters. His current live site uses them; this build does not,
  because the skill bans them outright. ✓

---

## Mobile: an authored decision, not a documented one

**`devices.md` and `taste.md` contain no mobile recipe for split stage.** I
checked both. This is a gap in the skill, and the decision below is mine, made
deliberately rather than discovered.

At 390px, two live columns would be ~180px each, which breaks the grammar's own
rule that neither column may become decorative.

**The rule for this build:** below 760px the split **rotates to horizontal.**

- Data side becomes the top band, question side the bottom band.
- The divider runs horizontally across the middle, and the force trace is drawn
  left-to-right along it instead of top-to-bottom.
- Both sides remain readable at once on the first screen. Grammar satisfied.
- The collapse still happens: the divider travels **up** to the top edge and the
  question band takes the full height.

The semantics are preserved — both sides present, both moving, one wins at the
end. Only the axis changes.

---

## Hard constraints carried in from his own work

- **No identifiable athlete data, ever.** The data wall is built from metric
  *names* and *categories* only (jump height, RSI-mod, ACWR, sprint splits, HRV,
  contact time). Any numeral shown is an unattributed sample, visibly not tied
  to a person, and never animated by a counter. `~/DEV/PERFORMANCE.md` marks this
  as handling-care material.
- **No em dashes in visible copy.** Skill rule, and it matches his own briefs.
- **No gradient text, no neon glow, no zero-offset halo shadows.**
- **`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** must leave the page fully readable and
  fully usable, with the trace drawn in its final state.

are not data problems. They are question problems."* Split stage is the grammar
for "any argument with two sides… the comparison is the product." Its mandated
close is the **collapse**: the divider travels to one edge, one column takes the
full width, and the CTA lives in the winning column. That collapse *is* the peak
he picked, unprompted. The grammar and the peak are the same object.

**Why the other seven lost.**

| Grammar | Why not |
|---|---|
| Filmic one-shot | Carries a burden of proof in this skill, and would need a scrub hero. No video exists. Its own strength — carrying the visitor — is wrong for a page whose point is that the visitor should stop and re-ask the question. |
| Chaptered editorial | Genuine runner-up. Fits a method or manifesto. Rejected because it has no structural home for the reframe: chapters cut, they do not resolve. The peak would become just another chapter opening. |
| Live surface | Requires panels that actually compute on real or clearly-labelled data. His real athlete data is identifiable health data and must never leave the machine. Without it the grammar's honesty rule makes it unavailable. |
| Continuous world | He explicitly chose distinct scenes over one unbroken world. Also the most fragile and expensive option, and there is no geography in the brief. |
| Typographic poster | Strong on "no assets", and nearly won. Rejected on loudness: it is one continuous hero moment at 40vw type, which contradicts his premium-minimal answer and his own kitsch ban. |
| Gallery / catalog | For "what are the options". His question is "should I believe you", which is the opposite. |
| Rhythmic cutlist | Speed and hard cuts. Directly against the quiet, exact vibe and the slow reframe. |

**What this grammar forbids, and I will honour:** full-bleed anything before the
resolve; centred copy; the corner-anchored hero; a symmetric close; either
column becoming decorative. Bans: `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, more than one
`scrub`, `drift`.

**Nav, hero, close, per the grammar:** No top bar. **The divider is the chrome**
— it carries both side labels and the progress of the argument. The hero
establishes the split at 50/50 on the first screen with both headlines readable
at once. The close is the collapse.

---

The vertical divider between the two columns is not a rule. It is a live
**counter-movement jump force-time curve**, drawn in Canvas, running the full
height of the page, and its playhead position is driven off `--sc-p`.

  unweighting dip, the braking rise, the propulsion peak, flight at zero, the
  landing spike. Not a decorative wiggle. `taste.md` forbids fake data and his
  V3 brief carries a kitsch ban.
- As the argument advances, the trace advances. The visitor is scrolling through
  a jump.
- At the collapse, the trace **flattens to a single straight underline** beneath
  the one surviving sentence. The instrument stops measuring and becomes
  punctuation.

**Why this is not a reskin.** It is not a kit device with new parameters. It is
bespoke Canvas in the page, driven off the custom property the engine publishes.
The engine is not touched.

**Not a duplicate of his existing site.** `~/DEV/Website/personal/index.html`
already has a `trace-panel` the visitor drags as a slider. That is a widget
inside a section. This is the page's chrome, it spans the whole document, and
the visitor never grabs it — scroll drives it. Different object, different
interaction.

---

## The journey (beats)

| # | Beat | What shifts |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recognition | Both sides named. The visitor sees the split and understands the format before scrolling. |
| 2 | Accumulation | The data side thickens. More metrics, tighter packing, more insistent. |
| 3 | Strain | The data side is now overwhelming and still has not answered anything. |
| 4 | The reframe | **PEAK.** The data drains. One sentence stands. |
| 5 | Method | What replaces it: the four checks that come before the first chart. |
| 6 | Commitment | One action. Email. |

Six beats. Total span target **9.5 viewport-heights** — deliberately outside the
13.6–13.8vh / 6–7 act band that the skill records as a fingerprint of its own
first four builds.

---

## The feeling curve

Written before the score table, per `feel.md`.

| Act | Feeling | What on screen causes it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recognised, slightly on guard | Both headlines legible at once. Neither side is winning yet. The trace sits at quiet stance. |
| 2 | Busy. Mildly impressed. | The left column fills with real metric names. The trace enters the unweighting dip. |
| 3 | Oppressed. It is too much and it means nothing. | Left column at maximum density, still no answer. The trace hits the braking rise. Left column is now visibly louder than the right, and the right has gone almost silent. **This is the authored silence.** |
| 4 | Relief, then clarity. | The data drains. The divider travels. One sentence at full width. The trace peaks at propulsion, then goes to flight. |
| 5 | Grounded, practical | Four checks, plainly set. The trace lands. |
| 6 | Settled | The trace is a flat underline. One link. |

No two adjacent acts carry the same feeling. Act 3 is quieter on the right
precisely so act 4 is the largest change on the page.

**The peak:** act 4. It gets the largest span by a visible margin (2.6vh against
a 1.2–1.6vh average) and the silence in act 3 in front of it.

**Authored silence:** the right column in act 3 drops to a single short line with
a lot of space. The verification pass must not read this as dead scroll — the
left column and the trace are both still moving through it.

**The tell-someone sentence:**
*"It's the site where all the data drains away and leaves you with the question."*

---

| Beat | Device | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Recognition | `pin` + divider at 50/50 | The grammar requires both headlines readable at once before any movement. Pin holds the frame while the split is understood. |
| 2 Accumulation | `flow` + `in` | Items arriving on their own schedule is what accumulation *is*. No pinning — the page should feel like it is filling, not holding. |
| 3 Strain | `reveal` (per side) | A wipe is a change of state. The left side wipes to its dense state; the right wipes down to almost nothing. |
| 4 The reframe | `pin` + `--sc-p` divider travel | The peak. Frame holds absolutely still while the divider crosses the whole viewport and the data drains. Stillness is what makes the travel readable. |
| 5 Method | `flow` + `in` | Back to arriving, but slower and in one column. Same family as act 2 on purpose — by now it reads as resolution, not repetition, because the layout changed underneath it. |
| 6 Commitment | `pin` + pointer | The page stops moving and starts responding. Grammar bans `magnet`, so the pointer work is a subtle cursor-proximity warm on the mail link only. |

- No two adjacent acts share a feeling. ✓
- One peak (act 4), largest span by a clear margin. ✓
- Total 9.5vh, six acts — outside the 13.6–13.8vh fingerprint band. ✓
- No `count` device anywhere: he has no real site statistics, and inventing them
  is banned. No number, no counter. ✓
- No `01 / 06` counters. His current live site uses them; this build does not,
  because the skill bans them outright. ✓

---

**`devices.md` and `taste.md` contain no mobile recipe for split stage.** I
checked both. This is a gap in the skill, and the decision below is mine, made
deliberately rather than discovered.

At 390px, two live columns would be ~180px each, which breaks the grammar's own
rule that neither column may become decorative.

**The rule for this build:** below 760px the split **rotates to horizontal.**

- Data side becomes the top band, question side the bottom band.

  left-to-right along it instead of top-to-bottom.
- Both sides remain readable at once on the first screen. Grammar satisfied.

  question band takes the full height.

The semantics are preserved — both sides present, both moving, one wins at the
end. Only the axis changes.

---

  *names* and *categories* only (jump height, RSI-mod, ACWR, sprint splits, HRV,
  contact time). Any numeral shown is an unattributed sample, visibly not tied
  to a person, and never animated by a counter. `~/DEV/PERFORMANCE.md` marks this
  as handling-care material.
- **No em dashes in visible copy.** Skill rule, and it matches his own briefs.
- **No gradient text, no neon glow, no zero-offset halo shadows.**

  fully usable, with the trace drawn in its final state.

# The taste floor

Read this before writing markup, not after. Build without announcing the
checklist.

Everything here is a check on the **rendered result**, not on intention. "I used
a spacing scale" is not evidence; a computed value is.

---

## Spacing

Rhythm comes from the contrast between tight and generous, never from one value
repeated until everything weighs the same. If you can't point at which intervals
are the tight ones and which are the breaks, the page has no rhythm.

- Use the 4px-base scale (`--sc-1` … `--sc-11`). A 4-base gives the useful
  middle steps an 8-only scale misses.
- **More space above a heading than below it.** The gap belongs to the boundary
  between sections, not to the heading-and-body pair. Getting this backwards is
  the single most common spacing error, and it makes a page read as a list.
- Section padding is fluid (`--sc-section`). A phone should not inherit desktop
  air; 8rem of padding on a 375px screen is a scroll tax.
- Group by proximity before reaching for a container. If you added a border to
  show two things are related, the spacing was wrong first.
- Gutters scale with viewport (`--sc-gutter`). Full-bleed media goes edge to
  edge; text never does.

**Optical, not mathematical.** Equal computed padding around a shape with
uneven visual weight looks wrong. Correct against the render, not the number.

---

## Typography

- **Two families maximum.** Display carries voice, text carries prose. A third
  is a costume.
- **Tracking tightens as size grows.** A face set at 6rem with default tracking
  reads loose and amateur. The ramp handles this: `--sc-track-tight` on display,
  `--sc-track-normal` on body. This is optical correction, not decoration.
- **Body measure 45 to 75ch.** `--sc-measure` is 62ch. A full-width paragraph on
  a 1600px monitor is unreadable regardless of font size.
- **Line height inverse to measure.** Wider lines need more leading. Display at
  0.94 to 1.06, body at 1.6.
- **Light text on dark needs compensation on three axes**: slightly more line
  height, a touch more tracking, one step more weight. Dark-mode type set with
  light-mode metrics looks thin and blurry, and this is why.
- `text-wrap: balance` on headings, `pretty` on body. Free, and it removes the
  orphan word that makes a headline look accidental.
- Display max ~6rem outside a genuine hero moment. Bigger is not more confident.
- **Step the hero down one rung below ~700px.** `--sc-t-4xl` floors at 3.4rem,
  which is a *desktop* floor: at 390px it wraps a normal hero headline to six
  lines. `--sc-t-2xl` on the hero inside a phone media query fixes it. The
  portrait crop of the image is covered in assets.md; this is the portrait crop
  of the type, and it is missed more often.

**Font choice.** Inter is discouraged as a default: it is the most-used face in
AI-generated pages and it reads as a non-decision. Reach first for Geist,
Archivo, Outfit, Satoshi, Cabinet Grotesk, or the brand's own face. Inter is
correct when the brand asks for neutral, or when accessibility is the brief.

**Serif is not a synonym for premium.** "It feels editorial" is not a reason.
Use one only when the brand names it, or when the work is genuinely editorial,
luxury, or heritage and you can say why *this* serif fits *this* brand.

**Emphasis inside a headline** uses italic or bold of the same family. Dropping
a serif word into a sans headline for visual interest is amateur.

---

## Colour

- **Six roles, one accent.** Canvas, surface, ink, ink-soft, accent, accent-ink.
  The accent owns a region or a role; scattered tiny accents are confetti.
- **Lock the accent for the whole page.** A warm-grey site does not grow a blue
  CTA in section seven. **The one exception is a page that hard-cuts between
  light and dark grounds**, which physically cannot clear 4.5:1 on both with a
  single stop. That page carries a two-stop accent: one hue, two lightnesses,
  keyed to the ground family, redefined per section alongside the ink. Still one
  accent per ground, and still one hue for the page. Two different hues is not
  what this licenses.
- **Secondary text is tinted, never flat gray.** Derive it from the foreground
  or surface hue. `#888` on a warm dark ground looks dirty.
- **No pure black.** `#000` has no air in it. Off-black at minimum.
- Contrast, measured on the render: body ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1, controls and
  focus indicators ≥3:1.
- Drift keeps the whole page in one theme family. See devices.md §10.

**Redefining `--sc-ink` on a subtree does not re-ink the text under it.**
`color` is inherited as a *computed value*, so text whose `color` already
resolved on `<body>` keeps the body's ink no matter what the section redefines
the token to. Every page that inverts a ground mid-page hits this, and it fails
silently: an inverted section renders bone type on concrete at 1.15:1 while the
harness correctly classifies the line as light-on-dark and grades it in the
wrong direction. The fix is one declaration on the same subtree:

```css
.section--light { --sc-ink: #14110C; --sc-ink-soft: #4A443A; color: var(--sc-ink); }
```

Restate `color` wherever you restate the token. The same applies to any other
inherited property you drive from a token on a subtree.

**The premium-consumer palette trap.** Warm cream background, brass or clay
accent, espresso near-black text is the default reach for every artisan, food,
wellness and craft brief, and it makes every such brand look identical. Do not
default to it. Rotate: cold silver and chrome; deep forest with bone and amber;
true off-black with warm tan; cobalt against a single neutral; olive with brick.
Use cream-and-brass only when the brand names those colours.

content.content:
/* ============================================================================ scrollcraft: a scroll-driven interaction runtime ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Vanilla JS. Zero dependencies. Zero DOM generation. The engine does NOT build your page. You author real, semantic HTML and mark it up with data-sc-* attributes; the engine reads them and drives them from a single scroll value on a single rAF loop. That is deliberate: a runtime that generates its own DOM from a config object makes every site it touches look identical, which is the failure mode this replaces. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ACTS: the unit of scroll time ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
...
data-sc-act scrub | pin | pan | flow (default: flow) data-sc-clip-map="travel" opts a pinned act OUT of full-life clip mapping. By DEFAULT a scrub clip is mapped across the stage's entire on-screen life, not across its pinned travel, because a pinned stage is visible for a viewport BEFORE the pin begins (sliding up into view) and a viewport AFTER it ends (sliding off the top). Mapped to pinned travel, the clip sits on its first frame through the whole entry and its last frame through the whole exit: the reader watches a still photograph while the page moves. Pair it with data-sc-dwell, which moves quickly at the edges and settles in the middle, so the fast motion lands on the two slides and the settle lands inside the pin where the copy is. data-sc-runout is accepted and ignored; it named the old opt-in for the exit half of this. data-sc-span viewport-heights of scroll this act owns. Pinned devices only (scrub/pin/pan). Default 1.5. The engine sets the outer height and sticks the first .sc-stage / [data-sc-stage] child. Every act exposes a normalized progress p (0..1): pinned p = (y - top) / (height - vh) flow p = (y + vh - top) / (height + vh) and publishes it as --sc-p on the act element, so CSS can read it too. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- DEVICES: what p drives --------------------------------------------------------------------------- data-sc-scrub on

input.command:
cat >> /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash/BRIEF.md <<'EOF'

---

## The feel check (run after the build, per feel.md §6)

Scrolled cold, one word per act written before opening this file, then diffed.

| Act | Intended | Felt | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recognised, on guard | Stated | Match. The two-column sentence does the work before any motion. |
| 2 | Busy, mildly impressed | Filling | Match. |
| 3 | Oppressed | Confronted | Match. "And?" at 8rem against forty-two dense chips is the whole beat. |
| 4 | Relief, then clarity | Released | Match, and it is the largest visual change on the page. |
| 5 | Grounded, practical | Practical | Match. |
| 6 | Settled | Settled | Match. The trace fades and the only accent left is the rule under the address. |

No act needed re-scoring. The curve as authored is the curve as felt.

---

## What was verified, and what was not

**Verified by the harness**, three passes each re-run after every fix
(`lab/shots4`, `lab/mobile4` at 390x844, `lab/reduced4`):

- 9.3 viewport-heights, four pinned acts plus two flow acts.
- No dead scroll on any pass.
- Every cue clears 4.5:1 at its worst frame on the composited page.

**Verified by reading the frames, which the harness cannot do:**

- The peak reads: the divider crosses, the wall drains, one sentence stands.
- The close resolves: the trace fades out and hands off to the rule under the
  address. Nothing trails away.
- Keyboard: both links reachable, neither parked at `opacity: 0`, both scrolled
  into view on focus. Heading order is one `h1`, then `h2`s in reading order,
  with the four checks as `h3`s beneath their `h2`.

**Two defects the harness passed and the frames caught:**

1. **The trace was a hairline on desktop.** A single pixel amplitude constant
   cannot serve a 1800px vertical axis and a 780px horizontal one. Amplitude is
   now proportional to the axis. The first contact sheet shows the old version:
   the signature move read as an accidental line.
2. **Reduced motion rendered the page collapsed from the first frame.** Driving
   the peak progress to 1 for the static state also drove the split to 8%, so
   the hero was clipped inside an 8vw column and unreadable. The harness passed
   it, because it grades cues and contrast rather than layout. Reduced motion
   now holds the readable 50/50 split and draws the full curve statically.

**Not verified:**

- **A real phone.** Every mobile result here is headless Chrome at 390x844. It
  cannot reproduce an iPhone's touch scrolling or Low Power Mode. There is no
  video in this build, so the usual iOS clip-lifecycle traps do not apply, but
  the rotated split and the horizontal trace should be looked at on a handset
  before this goes anywhere public.
- **Any hosting.** This build is a folder of files served locally. It is not
  published, and it does not touch the existing Artifact.
EOF

3	Interviewed 2026-09-02. Five of the eight answers are the human's own choices,

8	
9	---
10	
11	## The eight interview answers
12	
13	**1. Vibe in three to five words, plus references from any medium.**
14	*Self-authored, from BRIEF-V3.md.*
15	Quiet, exact, Texas, after-dark, instrumented.
16	References (non-web, per the skill's rule against naming sites):
17	- The instrument panel of a light aircraft at night — everything legible, nothing decorative.
18	- A Peter Saville record sleeve: one idea, enormous space around it.
19	- A stadium an hour after everyone leaves, floodlights still on.
20

22	*Self-authored, from the section headings of his live site, which are his own words.*
23	The question comes first → four checks before the first chart → what I actually
24	work with → how I work → get in touch.
25	
26	**3. The energy curve.**
27	*Self-authored.*
28	Starts quiet and slightly tense. Tightens through the middle as the data side
29	gets denser and more insistent. Releases hard at the reframe. Ends quiet, but a
30	different quiet from the opening: settled rather than waiting.
31	
32	**4. How should someone feel, stage by stage, and the ONE moment they remember?**
33	The one moment is **his own answer, chosen in-session**: *the question reframe.*
34	A wall of athlete data drains away and leaves one sentence standing.
35	Stage-by-stage feeling curve is below.

38	Seeded by his choice of peak. Realised as the signature move below.
39	
40	**6. How far from premium-minimal.**
41	**Premium-minimal.** His answer. Consistent with the kitsch ban in BRIEF-V3.md.
42	
43	**7. One unbroken world, or distinct scenes?**
44	**Distinct scenes.** His answer. Worldflight is therefore out, and so is the
45	continuous-world grammar.
46	
47	**8. What assets do they already have?**
48	**Nothing.** His answer. No photos, no footage, no brand imagery, and no
49	`KIE_AI_API_KEY` on the machine. He chose the code-drawn route over buying
50	credits. Every visual on this page is Canvas 2D or inline SVG, drawn in the
51	page. There is no video anywhere in this build.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Grammar: Split stage
56	
57	Two columns held in tension for the whole page, resolved by scroll.
58	
59	**Why this one.** His thesis has two literal sides — *"Most performance problems
60	are not data problems. They are question problems."* Split stage is the grammar
61	for "any argument with two sides… the comparison is the product." Its mandated
62	close is the **collapse**: the divider travels to one edge, one column takes the
63	full width, and the CTA lives in the winning column. That collapse *is* the peak
64	he picked, unprompted. The grammar and the peak are the same object.
65	
66	**Why the other seven lost.**
67	
68	| Grammar | Why not |
69	|---|---|
70	| Filmic one-shot | Carries a burden of proof in this skill, and would need a scrub hero. No video exists. Its own strength — carrying the visitor — is wrong for a page whose point is that the visitor should stop and re-ask the question. |
71	| Chaptered editorial | Genuine runner-up. Fits a method or manifesto. Rejected because it has no structural home for the reframe: chapters cut, they do not resolve. The peak would become just another chapter opening. |
72	| Live surface | Requires panels that actually compute on real or clearly-labelled data. His real athlete data is identifiable health data and must never leave the machine. Without it the grammar's honesty rule makes it unavailable. |
73	| Continuous world | He explicitly chose distinct scenes over one unbroken world. Also the most fragile and expensive option, and there is no geography in the brief. |
74	| Typographic poster | Strong on "no assets", and nearly won. Rejected on loudness: it is one continuous hero moment at 40vw type, which contradicts his premium-minimal answer and his own kitsch ban. |
75	| Gallery / catalog | For "what are the options". His question is "should I believe you", which is the opposite. |
76	| Rhythmic cutlist | Speed and hard cuts. Directly against the quiet, exact vibe and the slow reframe. |
77	
78	**What this grammar forbids, and I will honour:** full-bleed anything before the
79	resolve; centred copy; the corner-anchored hero; a symmetric close; either
80	column becoming decorative. Bans: `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, more than one
81	`scrub`, `drift`.
82	
83	**Nav, hero, close, per the grammar:** No top bar. **The divider is the chrome**
84	— it carries both side labels and the progress of the argument. The hero
85	establishes the split at 50/50 on the first screen with both headlines readable
86	at once. The close is the collapse.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## The signature move: the divider is a force trace
91	
92	The vertical divider between the two columns is not a rule. It is a live
93	**counter-movement jump force-time curve**, drawn in Canvas, running the full
94	height of the page, and its playhead position is driven off `--sc-p`.
95	
96	- It is drawn from the real, known shape of a CMJ trace: quiet stance, the
97	  unweighting dip, the braking rise, the propulsion peak, flight at zero, the
98	  landing spike. Not a decorative wiggle. `taste.md` forbids fake data and his
99	  V3 brief carries a kitsch ban.
100	- As the argument advances, the trace advances. The visitor is scrolling through
101	  a jump.
102	- At the collapse, the trace **flattens to a single straight underline** beneath
103	  the one surviving sentence. The instrument stops measuring and becomes
104	  punctuation.
105	
106	**Why this is not a reskin.** It is not a kit device with new parameters. It is
107	bespoke Canvas in the page, driven off the custom property the engine publishes.
108	The engine is not touched.
109	
110	**Not a duplicate of his existing site.** `~/DEV/Website/personal/index.html`
111	already has a `trace-panel` the visitor drags as a slider. That is a widget
112	inside a section. This is the page's chrome, it spans the whole document, and
113	the visitor never grabs it — scroll drives it. Different object, different
114	interaction.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## The journey (beats)
119	
120	| # | Beat | What shifts |
121	|---|---|---|
122	| 1 | Recognition | Both sides named. The visitor sees the split and understands the format before scrolling. |
123	| 2 | Accumulation | The data side thickens. More metrics, tighter packing, more insistent. |
124	| 3 | Strain | The data side is now overwhelming and still has not answered anything. |
125	| 4 | The reframe | **PEAK.** The data drains. One sentence stands. |
126	| 5 | Method | What replaces it: the four checks that come before the first chart. |
127	| 6 | Commitment | One action. Email. |
128	
129	Six beats. Total span target **9.5 viewport-heights** — deliberately outside the
130	13.6–13.8vh / 6–7 act band that the skill records as a fingerprint of its own
131	first four builds.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## The feeling curve
136	
137	Written before the score table, per `feel.md`.
138	
139	| Act | Feeling | What on screen causes it |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| 1 | Recognised, slightly on guard | Both headlines legible at once. Neither side is winning yet. The trace sits at quiet stance. |
142	| 2 | Busy. Mildly impressed. | The left column fills with real metric names. The trace enters the unweighting dip. |
143	| 3 | Oppressed. It is too much and it means nothing. | Left column at maximum density, still no answer. The trace hits the braking rise. Left column is now visibly louder than the right, and the right has gone almost silent. **This is the authored silence.** |
144	| 4 | Relief, then clarity. | The data drains. The divider travels. One sentence at full width. The trace peaks at propulsion, then goes to flight. |

It's built. **Look at it now:** http://localhost:4500 (the server is already running).

## What I made

A new site at `~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash/`.

Your old site is untouched. Same file, same Artifact link, not one byte changed.

## The idea

The skill made me pick one of eight page shapes. I picked **split stage**: two columns fighting for the whole page, one wins at the end.

I picked it because your own sentence already has two sides:

> **Left:** "Most performance problems are not data problems."
> **Right:** "They are question problems."

So the page starts split down the middle. The left side fills with metric names until it is a wall. The right side goes quiet, down to one word: **"And?"**

Then the wall drains away, the divider slides left, and one sentence takes the whole screen: **"The question comes first."**

Then your four checks, in your own words, pulled from your live site.

## The signature move

The line between the two columns is not a line. It is a **jump force trace** — a real countermovement jump curve. Quiet stance, the dip, the braking rise, the peak, flight, the landing spike.

You scroll, the trace advances. You are scrolling through a jump.

At the end it flattens and fades, and the only amber left on the page is the rule under your email address. The instrument stops measuring and becomes punctuation.

Nobody else can build that, because nobody else has your job.

## Did it work

Yes. Three screenshot passes, all green: desktop, phone, reduced-motion. No dead scroll. All text clears 4.5:1 contrast.

**But the robot passed two real bugs. I caught them by looking.**

1. The trace was a hairline on desktop. One fixed number cannot serve a tall screen and a wide phone. Now it scales.
2. **Reduced-motion was broken.** The page rendered already-collapsed, so the headline was squeezed into a sliver and unreadable. The checker passed it because it grades contrast, not layout. Fixed.

I also had to invent the phone layout. The skill has **no** mobile recipe for split stage. Below 760px I rotate it: data on top, question below, trace runs sideways. It works, and I wrote down that it was my call, not the skill's.

## What I could not check

**A real phone.** Everything mobile here is a fake phone in a headless browser. Look at it on your actual handset before showing anyone.

## What you do now

Nothing is required. It runs locally right now.

When you want it back later:

```
cd ~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash
node ~/.agents/skills/scroll-craft/scripts/serve.mjs --root . --port 4500
```

**One decision, 2 options:**

- **Leave it as a local draft.** Free. Look at it, decide if the idea holds. Your Artifact site stays your real site.
- **Put it online.** Needs a host and a domain. It is a plain folder of files, so any static host takes it.

I would leave it local for now. Sleep on it, open it tomorrow with fresh eyes, and see if the reframe still lands.

Everything I decided and why is in `BRIEF.md` in that folder, including the three interview answers I wrote for you instead of asking, since you were running on empty.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence (commit+push to KeystoneOS is standing-authorized per `feedback-auto-commit-push`; for any OTHER repo with changes, commit locally and list the push as an open item instead of pushing).

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` in every repo touched this session (check cwd first, then any repo mentioned in the conversation; if session context is thin, check `KeystoneOS` and any `DEV/` repo with commits dated today).
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- KeystoneOS: stage, commit with a descriptive message, push. Authorized.
- Other repos with changes: commit locally with a descriptive message; do NOT push without asking — list it in the final report instead.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Never push to a repo other than KeystoneOS without explicit approval.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

1	# BRIEF — Eric Rash, personal site (scroll-craft build #1)
2	
3	Interviewed 2026-09-02. Five of the eight answers are the human's own choices,
4	made in-session. Three are marked **self-authored** and were written from his
5	existing `~/DEV/Website/personal/BRIEF-V3.md` ("Night Field") because he was
6	explicitly working at low capacity and the skill permits a self-authored
7	fallback. Those three are flagged inline and in the final report.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## The eight interview answers
12	
13	**1. Vibe in three to five words, plus references from any medium.**
14	*Self-authored, from BRIEF-V3.md.*
15	Quiet, exact, Texas, after-dark, instrumented.
16	References (non-web, per the skill's rule against naming sites):
17	- The instrument panel of a light aircraft at night — everything legible, nothing decorative.
18	- A Peter Saville record sleeve: one idea, enormous space around it.
19	- A stadium an hour after everyone leaves, floodlights still on.
20	
21	**2. The scroll journey, section by section.**
22	*Self-authored, from the section headings of his live site, which are his own words.*
23	The question comes first → four checks before the first chart → what I actually
24	work with → how I work → get in touch.
25	
26	**3. The energy curve.**
27	*Self-authored.*
28	Starts quiet and slightly tense. Tightens through the middle as the data side
29	gets denser and more insistent. Releases hard at the reframe. Ends quiet, but a
30	different quiet from the opening: settled rather than waiting.
31	
32	**4. How should someone feel, stage by stage, and the ONE moment they remember?**
33	The one moment is **his own answer, chosen in-session**: *the question reframe.*
34	A wall of athlete data drains away and leaves one sentence standing.
35	Stage-by-stage feeling curve is below.
36	
37	**5. One thing this site should do that no site they have seen does.**
38	Seeded by his choice of peak. Realised as the signature move below.
39	
40	**6. How far from premium-minimal.**
41	**Premium-minimal.** His answer. Consistent with the kitsch ban in BRIEF-V3.md.
42	
43	**7. One unbroken world, or distinct scenes?**
44	**Distinct scenes.** His answer. Worldflight is therefore out, and so is the
45	continuous-world grammar.
46	
47	**8. What assets do they already have?**
48	**Nothing.** His answer. No photos, no footage, no brand imagery, and no
49	`KIE_AI_API_KEY` on the machine. He chose the code-drawn route over buying
50	credits. Every visual on this page is Canvas 2D or inline SVG, drawn in the
51	page. There is no video anywhere in this build.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Grammar: Split stage
56	
57	Two columns held in tension for the whole page, resolved by scroll.
58	
59	**Why this one.** His thesis has two literal sides — *"Most performance problems
60	are not data problems. They are question problems."* Split stage is the grammar
61	for "any argument with two sides… the comparison is the product." Its mandated
62	close is the **collapse**: the divider travels to one edge, one column takes the
63	full width, and the CTA lives in the winning column. That collapse *is* the peak
64	he picked, unprompted. The grammar and the peak are the same object.
65	
66	**Why the other seven lost.**
67	
68	| Grammar | Why not |
69	|---|---|
70	| Filmic one-shot | Carries a burden of proof in this skill, and would need a scrub hero. No video exists. Its own strength — carrying the visitor — is wrong for a page whose point is that the visitor should stop and re-ask the question. |
71	| Chaptered editorial | Genuine runner-up. Fits a method or manifesto. Rejected because it has no structural home for the reframe: chapters cut, they do not resolve. The peak would become just another chapter opening. |
72	| Live surface | Requires panels that actually compute on real or clearly-labelled data. His real athlete data is identifiable health data and must never leave the machine. Without it the grammar's honesty rule makes it unavailable. |
73	| Continuous world | He explicitly chose distinct scenes over one unbroken world. Also the most fragile and expensive option, and there is no geography in the brief. |
74	| Typographic poster | Strong on "no assets", and nearly won. Rejected on loudness: it is one continuous hero moment at 40vw type, which contradicts his premium-minimal answer and his own kitsch ban. |
75	| Gallery / catalog | For "what are the options". His question is "should I believe you", which is the opposite. |
76	| Rhythmic cutlist | Speed and hard cuts. Directly against the quiet, exact vibe and the slow reframe. |
77	
78	**What this grammar forbids, and I will honour:** full-bleed anything before the
79	resolve; centred copy; the corner-anchored hero; a symmetric close; either
80	column becoming decorative. Bans: `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, more than one
81	`scrub`, `drift`.
82	
83	**Nav, hero, close, per the grammar:** No top bar. **The divider is the chrome**
84	— it carries both side labels and the progress of the argument. The hero
85	establishes the split at 50/50 on the first screen with both headlines readable
86	at once. The close is the collapse.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## The signature move: the divider is a force trace
91	
92	The vertical divider between the two columns is not a rule. It is a live
93	**counter-movement jump force-time curve**, drawn in Canvas, running the full
94	height of the page, and its playhead position is driven off `--sc-p`.
95	
96	- It is drawn from the real, known shape of a CMJ trace: quiet stance, the
97	  unweighting dip, the braking rise, the propulsion peak, flight at zero, the
98	  landing spike. Not a decorative wiggle. `taste.md` forbids fake data and his
99	  V3 brief carries a kitsch ban.
100	- As the argument advances, the trace advances. The visitor is scrolling through
101	  a jump.
102	- At the collapse, the trace **flattens to a single straight underline** beneath
103	  the one surviving sentence. The instrument stops measuring and becomes
104	  punctuation.
105	
106	**Why this is not a reskin.** It is not a kit device with new parameters. It is
107	bespoke Canvas in the page, driven off the custom property the engine publishes.
108	The engine is not touched.
109	
110	**Not a duplicate of his existing site.** `~/DEV/Website/personal/index.html`
111	already has a `trace-panel` the visitor drags as a slider. That is a widget
112	inside a section. This is the page's chrome, it spans the whole document, and
113	the visitor never grabs it — scroll drives it. Different object, different
114	interaction.
115	
116	---

118	## The journey (beats)
119	
120	| # | Beat | What shifts |
121	|---|---|---|
122	| 1 | Recognition | Both sides named. The visitor sees the split and understands the format before scrolling. |
123	| 2 | Accumulation | The data side thickens. More metrics, tighter packing, more insistent. |
124	| 3 | Strain | The data side is now overwhelming and still has not answered anything. |
125	| 4 | The reframe | **PEAK.** The data drains. One sentence stands. |
126	| 5 | Method | What replaces it: the four checks that come before the first chart. |
127	| 6 | Commitment | One action. Email. |
128	
129	Six beats. Total span target **9.5 viewport-heights** — deliberately outside the
130	13.6–13.8vh / 6–7 act band that the skill records as a fingerprint of its own
131	first four builds.

# Handoff — 2026-09-02 — scroll-craft install + first build

Plain markdown. Any harness (Codex, Antigravity, fresh Claude) should be able to
resume from this without the original session.

---

## What this session did

Three things, in order:

1. Installed the third-party **scroll-craft** skill across Claude Code, Codex and
   (packaged for) Claude Cowork.
2. Watched a 16-minute video that is the same author's method for using it, and
   distilled it into redesign notes for Eric's personal site.
3. Ran scroll-craft for real and produced **build #1**, a standalone site.

---

## 1. scroll-craft install

Source: <https://github.com/nateherkai/scroll-craft> (MIT, plugin `nateherk-design`).

Installed with the machine's existing `skills` CLI, which is what owns
`~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`:

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add nateherkai/scroll-craft -g -a claude-code -a codex -s scroll-craft -y
```

**Gotcha:** the `-a` flag rejects a comma-separated list. `-a claude-code,codex`
errors with "Invalid agents" even though both names are valid. Repeat the flag.

Where it landed:

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `~/.agents/skills/scroll-craft/` | the real files (canonical vendor store) |
| `~/.claude/skills/scroll-craft` | symlink, made by the installer |
| `~/.codex/skills/scroll-craft` | symlink, **made by hand** — the installer reported "universal: Codex" and created nothing |
| `~/Downloads/scroll-craft.zip` | Cowork upload package |

**Cowork is not installed.** Cowork's skills carry server-minted ids
(`skill_01…`) in
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/.../manifest.json`,
so a folder dropped in locally is not registered and would be wiped on the next
sync. The only route is uploading the zip via claude.ai → Settings →
Capabilities → Skills. **This is still open — Eric has not done it.**
Expect the design procedure to work in Cowork but not the ffmpeg/Chrome
verification pass.

**Mac readiness:** `node ~/.agents/skills/scroll-craft/scripts/doctor.mjs` passes.
Node 26.6, full ffmpeg (490 filters), Chrome found. Optional gaps: no
`KIE_AI_API_KEY`, no libwebp encoder (posters fall back to JPEG). The README
claims the skill has only ever run on Windows; it runs on this Mac.

**Workspace:** resolves to `~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft` via the nearest `.git`
(which is `~/DEV/Website`). Registry at
`~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/FINGERPRINTS.md`. Run scroll-craft from inside
`~/DEV/Website/...` or set `SCROLLCRAFT_HOME`, otherwise builds land wherever
cwd happens to be, including inside the skill directory.

---

## 2. The `/watch` skill was broken, and is now patched

`/watch` returned **0 frames with no useful error**. Cause: `frames.py` passes
ffmpeg `-vsync`, which ffmpeg removed. This machine runs ffmpeg 9.0.1.

Fixed by hand in the two live copies (`-vsync` → `-fps_mode`, lines 256 and 615):

- `~/.agents/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py`
- `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-video/watch/0.2.0/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py`

Verified after the fix: scene path 8 frames, keyframe path 8 frames, 0 errors.

**This fix is temporary.** Upstream `bradautomates/claude-video` still has
`-vsync` (last commit 2026-06-30), so `skills update watch` or a plugin update
reinstalls the bug. The Cowork copy at
`…/skills-plugin/.../skills/watch/scripts/frames.py` was deliberately **not**
patched: it is server-synced and would revert.

Open, not done: offering an upstream PR. Eric was asked and has not answered.

---

## 3. Design notes from the video

`~/DEV/Website/personal/DESIGN-IDEAS.md` — distilled from
<https://youtu.be/FFWtxjvW2ts> (Nate Herk, "Fable 5.1 FINALLY Kills AI Website
Slop", 16:13). Same author as the skill; the video is the method, the skill is
the method in code.

The load-bearing points: you cannot ask a model for "premium", you must hand it
a **named element from a named reference**; his seven rules; four inspiration
sources (21st.dev, godly.design, Awwwards, motion-sites).

**The finding that matters most for Eric:** his live site
(`~/DEV/Website/personal/index.html`, published as a Claude Artifact) **cannot
run scroll-craft**. `BRIEF-V3.md` forbids external resources, libraries and
anything parked at `opacity: 0`; scroll-craft needs an engine JS/CSS pair,
external video, and scroll-assembled text. Section 6 of DESIGN-IDEAS.md lays
out the two ways forward. Eric chose **build standalone, leave the Artifact
alone** — which is what build #1 is.

Also corrected in that file: an earlier draft wrongly claimed his hero "leads
with role, not pain". It does not. It leads with *"Most performance problems are
not data problems. They are question problems."* and he already has a
scroll-driven jump-trace scrub. Two of the video's seven rules were already
satisfied before this session started.

---

## 4. Build #1 — `~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash/`

Serve it:

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash
node ~/.agents/skills/scroll-craft/scripts/serve.mjs --root . --port 4500
```

**Interview answers (his, in-session):** standalone build, distinct scenes,
premium-minimal, no assets and no kie.ai spend, peak = "the question reframe",
CTA = email. Three of the eight answers were **self-authored** from
`BRIEF-V3.md` because he was working at low capacity; they are flagged inline in
the build's `BRIEF.md` and the skill permits this fallback.

**Grammar: split stage.** Chosen because his thesis is literally a two-column
sentence, and the grammar's mandated close (the collapse) *is* the peak he
picked independently. Full reasoning for why the other seven lost is in
`builds/eric-rash/BRIEF.md`.

**Signature move:** the divider between the columns is a live **countermovement
jump force-time curve** in Canvas, full page height, advancing with scroll,
flattening and fading at the close so the last accent on the page is the rule
under his email address. Drawn from the real CMJ phase shape (quiet stance,
unweighting dip, braking rise, propulsion, flight, landing spike) — not a
decorative wiggle, and no numeric value is printed or attributed anywhere.

**Data-handling constraint honoured:** the "data wall" is metric *names* only.
No athlete named, no value attributed, no `count` device anywhere, because none
of those numbers would be real. `~/DEV/PERFORMANCE.md` marks athlete data as
handling-care material.

**The engine was never edited.** `scrollcraft.js` and `scrollcraft.css` in the
build folder are byte-identical to the skill's copies. All bespoke behaviour is
page-level JS driven off `--sc-p`.

### Verification

Three passes, all green after fixes (`lab/shots4`, `lab/mobile4` at 390×844,
`lab/reduced4`): 9.3 viewport-heights, no dead scroll, every cue clears 4.5:1.
Keyboard focus reaches both links, neither parked at opacity 0. Heading order is
clean.

**Two defects the harness passed and reading the frames caught:**

1. The trace was a hairline on desktop — one pixel constant cannot serve a
   1800px vertical axis and a 780px horizontal one. Amplitude is now
   proportional to the axis.
2. **Reduced motion rendered the page collapsed from the first frame**, clipping
   the hero inside an 8vw column. The harness passed it because it grades cues
   and contrast, not layout. Reduced motion now holds the readable 50/50 split.

**Mobile is an authored decision, not a documented one.** Neither `devices.md`
nor `taste.md` has a mobile recipe for split stage. Below 760px the split
rotates to horizontal (data on top, question beneath, trace drawn left to
right); the collapse travels upward instead of leftward. Written up in the
build's BRIEF.md.

**Not verified: a real phone.** All mobile results are headless Chrome. There is
no video in this build so the usual iOS clip traps do not apply, but the rotated
split should be looked at on a handset before this is shown to anyone.

---

## Every file created or modified this session

**Committed to `~/DEV/Website` (this repo, local only — not pushed):**

- `.gitignore` — new. Ignores `node_modules/` and `lab/`; the lab screenshots
  had reached 339MB across 292 PNGs and must never enter git.
- `personal/DESIGN-IDEAS.md` — new, the video notes.
- `personal/index.html`, `personal/BRIEF*.md` — **pre-existing and untouched by
  this session**, but never previously committed, so they enter git in this
  commit for the first time.
- `scrollcraft/FINGERPRINTS.md` — new registry, seeded plus the build #1 row.
- `scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash/{BRIEF.md,index.html,scrollcraft.js,scrollcraft.css,package.json,package-lock.json}`
- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-02-scroll-craft-eric-rash.md` — this file.

**Outside any repo:**

- `~/DEV/PERSONAL.md` — router line for `Website/` updated to name the new briefs
  and DESIGN-IDEAS.md.
- `~/.agents/skills/scroll-craft/` — installed.
- `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — installer added the scroll-craft entry.
- `~/.claude/skills/scroll-craft`, `~/.codex/skills/scroll-craft` — symlinks.
- `~/.agents/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py` — `-vsync` → `-fps_mode`.
- `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-video/watch/0.2.0/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py` — same.
- `~/Downloads/scroll-craft.zip` — Cowork upload package.
- `~/DEV/Website/scrollcraft/builds/eric-rash/lab/` — 292 verification PNGs,
  gitignored, reproducible with the Step 5 commands in the build's BRIEF.md.

---

## Next actions, most important first

1. **Look at build #1 on a real phone.** It is the one thing the verification
   could not cover.
2. **Decide: keep build #1 local, or host it.** Eric's site is currently an
   Artifact and stays that way either way. Recommendation given: leave it local,
   look again with fresh eyes before committing to a direction.
3. **Upload `~/Downloads/scroll-craft.zip` to Cowork** if Cowork parity is still
   wanted. One manual step, claude.ai → Settings → Capabilities → Skills.
4. **Push `~/DEV/Website`** to `origin` (`erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`) if
   the personal site and the scroll-craft build should be on GitHub. Not pushed
   this session — the repo is not KeystoneOS, so it needs explicit approval, and
   note this commit publishes `personal/index.html` for the first time.
5. **Consider an upstream PR** for the `/watch` `-vsync` fix, else it returns on
   the next update.

## Open questions

- Does Eric want the personal site source on GitHub at all? It has never been
  committed, which may have been deliberate.
- Upstream PR for `/watch`: offered, unanswered.
- Whether build #1's direction is right. It was built from three self-authored
  interview answers; if the vibe is off, that is the first place to look.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the retired Windows slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Never write to a `C--Users-eric-rash*` slug.** Those are pre-migration Windows keys from the box retired 2026-08-14. They are still indexed by memsearch, so old facts stay recallable, but nothing written there will ever be auto-injected again.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

---
name: vendored-skill-install
description: Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different
metadata:
  type: project
---

Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files, ~360 of
them) with `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
directories are symlinks into it:

- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → absolute path into `~/.agents/skills/`

Install with the CLI that owns that store, not by hand-copying:

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
```

**Trap: `-a` will not take a comma-separated list.** `-a claude-code,codex`
fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.

**Trap: the installer does not always wire Codex.** It reports
`universal: Codex` and creates no symlink. Check
`ls -l ~/.codex/skills/<name>` after every install and make the symlink by hand
if it is missing.

The CLI runs a security scan and may report alerts. Read
`https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>` before trusting a skill.

**Cowork cannot take a locally-dropped skill.** Its store is
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<a>/<b>/skills/`
with a sibling `manifest.json`, and every entry carries a **server-minted id**
(`skill_01…`). A folder placed there is not in the manifest and is wiped on the
next sync. The only route is a zip uploaded through claude.ai → Settings →
Capabilities → Skills, with the skill folder at the zip root. Expect Cowork's
sandbox to lack ffmpeg/Chrome, so any skill's verification or media step will
not run there even after a successful upload.

Where a skill puts its *output* is separate: some resolve a workspace from the
nearest `.git` walking up, so run them from inside the target project or set
their env override, or builds land wherever cwd happened to be.

See [[vendored-skill-repair]] for what to do when one of these is broken, and
[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]] before deleting any copy.

---
name: vendored-skill-repair
description: A vendored skill fails silently or with a confusing error — check for removed ffmpeg flags first, patch every live copy, and expect the fix to revert on update
metadata:
  type: project
---

When a third-party skill produces **empty output rather than an error**, suspect
a CLI flag the underlying tool has since removed, not the skill's own logic.

**The instance (2026-09-02):** `/watch` returned zero frames with no useful
message. Cause: `frames.py` passed ffmpeg `-vsync`, removed in ffmpeg 7+. This
machine runs **ffmpeg 9.0.1**. Fix is `-vsync` → `-fps_mode` (same `vfr` value,
same position, exists since ffmpeg 5.0).

**Patch every live copy, and know which ones matter.** A skill can exist three
times on this machine:

1. `~/.agents/skills/<name>/…` — the vendor store, serves `~/.claude/skills/` and Codex.
2. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<plugin>/<skill>/<version>/skills/<name>/…` — the
   plugin copy. **This is the one a `/slash` invocation actually loads.** Patch
   only the vendor store and the skill stays broken.
3. The Cowork copy under `Library/Application Support/Claude/…` — **do not
   patch.** It is server-synced and reverts. See [[vendored-skill-install]].

Confirm which file is live by reading the "Base directory for this skill" line
the harness prints when the skill loads.

**Every such patch is temporary.** Check upstream before assuming a fix is
needed, and after patching, assume `skills update` or a plugin update reinstalls

When a third-party skill produces **empty output rather than an error**, suspect
a CLI flag the underlying tool has since removed, not the skill's own logic.

**The instance (2026-09-02):** `/watch` returned zero frames with no useful
message. Cause: `frames.py` passed ffmpeg `-vsync`, removed in ffmpeg 7+. This
machine runs **ffmpeg 9.0.1**. Fix is `-vsync` → `-fps_mode` (same `vfr` value,
same position, exists since ffmpeg 5.0).

**Patch every live copy, and know which ones matter.** A skill can exist three
times on this machine:

1. `~/.agents/skills/<name>/…` — the vendor store, serves `~/.claude/skills/` and Codex.
2. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<plugin>/<skill>/<version>/skills/<name>/…` — the
   plugin copy. **This is the one a `/slash` invocation actually loads.** Patch
   only the vendor store and the skill stays broken.
3. The Cowork copy under `Library/Application Support/Claude/…` — **do not
   patch.** It is server-synced and reverts. See [[vendored-skill-install]].

Confirm which file is live by reading the "Base directory for this skill" line
the harness prints when the skill loads.

**Every such patch is temporary.** Check upstream before assuming a fix is
needed, and after patching, assume `skills update` or a plugin update reinstalls
the bug. For `/watch` the upstream is `bradautomates/claude-video`, still
carrying `-vsync` as of its 2026-06-30 commit.

Verify by running the affected code path and **counting the output**, not by
reading the exit code — the original failure exited 0.
